Create a new sd_data object

Source: R/class.R
new_sd_data.Rd

Internal constructor for the sd_data class, which bundles a survey dataset together with metadata about it (variable roles, labels, missing-value codes, and paradata such as fielding dates or response rate). Pipeline functions such as sd_summarise(), sd_document(), sd_generate_roxygen() and sd_codebook() all take an sd_data object as input.

Usage

new_sd_data(data, meta = list())

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble containing the survey data.

meta

A list of metadata. See Details for the expected structure.

Value

An object of class sd_data.

Details

meta is a list with (at least) these elements:

roles

Named character vector mapping variable names to a role: one of "id", "likert", "nominal", "continuous", "date", "text", "weight", or "unknown".

labels

Named list mapping variable names to a human-readable label.

value_labels

Named list mapping variable names to a named vector of value labels (value = name).

missing_codes

Named list mapping variable names to a vector of sentinel codes that should be treated as missing.

paradata

A list of dataset-level metadata, e.g. collection_mode, fieldwork, response_rate, sampling_frame.

If meta$labels/meta$value_labels are not supplied, they are harvested automatically from any label/labels attributes already present on data's columns (the same haven-style convention sd_read() uses for SPSS/Stata files) — see sd_harvest_attr_labels_(). This means a data.frame that already carries these attributes (e.g. one saved to .rds from a previous haven session, or shipped as a package's built-in example data) gets its labels picked up even when it isn't read in via sd_read()'s .sav/.dta path. Pass meta = list(labels = list(), value_labels = list()) explicitly to opt out and start with no labels regardless of what data's attributes contain.
